title: Console permission surface: granular role templates, effective-permissions preview, and member assignment flows
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: RBAC v1 in Console exposes only coarse role buckets and makes it hard for admins to understand the effective permissions a user will have when assigned multiple roles or role templates. We need a UI that supports: 1) creating and editing granular role templates (grouped by functional surface: inference, billing, infra, audit), 2) previewing effective permissions when adding roles to a member (including inherited and conflicting permissions), 3) clear, contextual warnings for high-risk permissions (modify billing, impersonate tokens, org-wide admin), 4) bulk member assignment flows with undo and audit trail links, and 5) keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly interactions for accessibility.
design_goals: Make permission scope boundaries explicit and scannable
Prevent accidental grant of high-risk privileges via warnings and friction
Provide a quick way to preview effective permissions for a member prior to commit
Support both individual and bulk assignment workflows with clear feedback
Keep patterns consistent with existing Console components and global search
acceptance_criteria: Role editor: allow creation of role templates with grouped permission toggles (group labels: Inference, Models, Billing, Console Admin, Observability, Audit)
Role editor: each permission includes an inline help tooltip that links to the RBAC reference docs
Member assignment modal: shows immediate effective-permissions preview that updates as roles are toggled
Member assignment: highlights conflicts and shows a concise explanation (e.g., role A grants create-model; role B denies create-model -> show resolution policy)
Bulk assignment: support uploading CSV with email and role columns; show preview rows, validation errors and a one-click undo after apply
High-risk action prevention: for actions that grant org-level admin or billing-modify, show a mandatory confirmation step and record selection reason in the audit message
Audit integration: every role change includes a link to a generated audit log entry (or placeholder when offline) and populates change metadata for the observability console
Accessibility: all interactive elements are keyboard navigable, role toggles announce state to screen readers and color is not the sole indicator of state
E2E flows: PM/Eng acceptance tests that create role templates, assign to users, and validate effective permission on a test org
arch_notes_for_engineering: Frontend should compute effective permissions client-side using the RBAC decision matrix from ENG-4187; fallback to server when dataset exceeds limit
Expose an API endpoint for CSV validation and dry-run assignment (ENG-4187/ENG-4199 collaboration)
Include a debounce on permission preview updates to avoid overloading the kernel when toggling many roles
Audit message payload must include actor, timestamp, changeset diff, and the optional admin-provided reason
acceptance_test_steps: 1) Create role template 'Model Operator' with permissions: models.read, models.create, inference.run
2) Create role template 'Cost Auditor' with permissions: billing.read, billing.estimate
3) Open member assignment modal, add user jessica@acme.com and assign both templates; verify preview shows combined permissions
4) Assign a second role that includes a deny for models.create and confirm UI shows conflict resolution rationale
5) Upload a CSV with 10 rows, fix validation errors in preview, apply and then use undo to revert one batch operation
6) Grant org-level admin to test user and confirm mandatory confirmation modal requires typed org name and reason; verify audit link appears
notes: Avoid replicating the old roles matrix screen — this is a guided, contextual editor with previews
Consider a compact 'role chip' that reveals scope on hover and opens the role editor on click
Edge case: external SSO groups may map to roles; show mapping in member preview and surface origin (SCIM / SAML)
open_questions: How should deny rules be modeled in the UI vs. backend? (explicit deny vs. precedence ordering)
Do we allow admins to define custom resolution policies when conflicts occur or stick to a single server-side precedence model?
Should bulk CSV uploads be restricted to Dedicated/Enterprise customers initially?
comments: 2026-02-19 - Maya Chen: Initial discovery and stakeholder interviews complete. PM expressed strong preference for an 'effective permissions' preview. Action: prototype low-fi preview in Figma.
2026-02-25 - Arjun Patel: Built initial lo-fi and tested with 3 customers in user research. Feedback: preview is valuable but warnings felt buried; moving confirmation out of secondary modal.
2026-03-02 - Priya Menon (PM): Added requirement to persist admin-provided reason into audit logs for compliance. Raised dependency on ENG-4199 for audit schema changes.
2026-03-04 - Security (Evan Ruiz): Recommended mandatory security_review_required for templates that include billing.* or org.* permissions. Flagged potential policy enforcement via SSO attributes.
